newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cancels meeting with Milosevic.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cancels meeting with Milosevic.

text.p: The United States has cancelled a meeting with Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to intensify pressure on the Belgrade government over anti-democratic moves, officials said on Monday.

They said that Assistant Secretary of State John Kornblum, the special envoy on Bosnia, had been scheduled to meet Milosevic in Belgrade later this week after a NATO meeting but had decided to call off the visit.

"We've already cancelled one visit to Belgrade and that was John Kornblum (who) was set to go out and talk to Milosevic after the NATO meetings in Brussels...That's one action that's going to be taken," one senior official said.

"We're cutting him (Milosevic) off little by little," said the official, adding: "Basically he's doing it because he doesn't think it's useful to talk to Milosevic at this particular moment...It's in reaction to recent events, absolutely."
Kornblum acted after Serbia's top court awarded control of Belgrade city council to the ruling Socialists after an election that the opposition is widely viewed as having won.
The decision also followed reports of the beating in prison of Dejan Bulatovic, 21, a worker who was arrested on Friday for carrying an effigy of Milosevic in prison garb.
